role_sought: Member of the Sejm, Gdańsk constituency (no. 22), Liberal Democratic Congress (KLD) list
detail: The KLD, which Tusk co-founded, won 37 seats nationally.

role_sought: Member of the Sejm, constituency no. 11, KLD list
detail: Despite a strong personal result he lost his seat because the KLD failed to reach the 5% national threshold.
Subsequently chosen as a Deputy Marshal of the Senate for the 1997–2001 term.

role_sought: Member of the Sejm, Gdynia constituency (no. 26), Civic Platform list
detail: First election contested by the newly founded Civic Platform; Tusk then became a Deputy Marshal of the Sejm.

role_sought: Member of the Sejm, Gdańsk constituency (no. 25), Civic Platform list
detail: PiS won the election with 26.99% to PO's 24.14%, and planned PO–PiS coalition talks collapsed; PO went into opposition.

role_sought: President of the Republic of Poland
result: First place; advanced to the run-off
detail: Tusk led the first round ahead of Lech Kaczyński.

role_sought: President of the Republic of Poland
detail: Turnout was about 51%. The campaign featured a controversy over a claim by PiS politician Jacek Kurski that Tusk's grandfather had volunteered for the Wehrmacht; according to the record cited by Polish Wikipedia, he had been conscripted in 1944 as a resident of the annexed Free City of Danzig.

role_sought: Member of the Sejm, Warsaw constituency (no. 19), and PO candidate for Prime Minister
detail: The early election ended the PiS-led government; Tusk formed a PO–PSL coalition and became Prime Minister on 16 November 2007.

role_sought: Member of the Sejm, Warsaw constituency (no. 19), and PO candidate for Prime Minister
detail: PO became the first ruling party re-elected since 1989, and Tusk the first re-elected Prime Minister; the PO–PSL coalition continued.

election: Election of the President of the European Council
detail: Chosen by EU heads of state or government at a special European Council meeting; took office on 1 December 2014.

election: Re-election of the President of the European Council
role_sought: President of the European Council (second term)
opponent: Jacek Saryusz-Wolski (nominated by Poland's PiS government)
detail: Poland's own government opposed his re-election and was the only member state to vote against.

election: EPP Congress, Zagreb — election of the party president
role_sought: President of the European People's Party
detail: Took office on 1 December 2019, the day after his European Council term ended.
Confirmed as PO leader after returning to Polish politics in July 2021 as acting chairman.

role_sought: Member of the Sejm, Warsaw constituency (no. 19), heading the Civic Coalition (KO) list
result: Elected; KO second, opposition coalition won a majority
detail: PiS came first but lost its majority; KO, Third Way and The Left together won 248 of 460 seats and formed a government under Tusk.

election: Sejm vote electing the Prime Minister (Article 154(3) of the Constitution)
detail: Held the same day Mateusz Morawiecki's government lost its confidence vote; the Sejm approved Tusk's cabinet on 12 December and it was sworn in on 13 December 2023.

election: Sejm vote of confidence in the Tusk government
role_sought: Prime Minister (confidence vote requested by the government)
detail: Tusk sought the vote after his coalition's candidate Rafał Trzaskowski lost the June 2025 presidential run-off to Karol Nawrocki.

role_sought: Chairman of the Civic Coalition party
detail: First leadership vote of the KO party formed in October 2025 from PO, Nowoczesna and Inicjatywa Polska; results announced on 9 March 2026.
